source.title: Rethinking Refusal Directions: Identification and Intervention Effects

record.tranche_reason: It constructs harmful-minus-benign activation-contrast directions and tests directional ablation and addition on new instruction-tuned checkpoints. The all-layer ablation is limited to prompt prefill, and the formal direction-selection procedure differs from the original.
record.gate_note: The direction-identity tables report operational selection outcomes; they are included as measurements of the constructed direction, not as evidence that either objective uniquely recovers an internal axis. The paper also reports continuous first-token proxy analyses, but these are distinct from semantic refusal and are not recorded as behavioral results for V1. Values used only in selecting directions and diagnostic generation-time qualification runs are not recorded as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: It builds harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference directions for four new instruct checkpoints. It then applies all-layer directional ablation and activation addition, measuring full-generation semantic refusal on harmful and benign prompts. Interventions are prefill-only, unlike the original, which also intervenes during decoding.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that semantic d′ stays positive in every model–dataset condition, so harmful–benign selectivity persists under prefill interventions. They note this does not rule out direction information being used again during decoding.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-benign activation-contrast candidates and all-layer directional ablation, but selects directions with a Wang-style procedure, evaluates full-generation semantic judgments, and restricts formal interventions to prompt prefill rather than continuing the intervention during decoding.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction identity varies with selection objective (notably for Qwen 2.5–3B); intervention effects vary by operator, checkpoint, dose, and prompt population. WildGuardTest and XSTest show different baseline regimes and intervention responses.

fits_no_version.finding: Which harmful-minus-harmless candidate is selected depends on the selection objective. Cosine between the Wang and COSMIC winners ranges 1.000 to 0.089 (Qwen 3B: rank 102/180). The lexical proxy shifts the selected Gemma 9B layer (cosine 0.356).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The identity of the selected refusal direction depends on the selection objective and refusal proxy.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a CAA first-token proxy, a common displacement produces prompt-specific local gains that predict proxy discrimination better than class or global gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering along a refusal direction has heterogeneous per-prompt downstream gain.

record.problems: Only four instruction-tuned checkpoints and two prompt datasets are tested. Formal interventions are prefill-only, so the study does not assess repeated intervention during decoding. Semantic d′ is descriptive and does not establish equal-variance latent sensitivity. The local-gain analysis uses a first-token proxy with no assumption-free bridge to semantic refusal. The authors note that the follow-up inferential radius was selected after inspection rather than preregistered.
record.rows_left_out: The lexical-proxy audit in Table 1 is not included as separate rows; the same-bank cross-objective comparison in Table 2 captures the direction-identity result most directly. Most individual CAA and scaling dose effects from Appendix K, Table 17 are omitted to stay focused on the claim's core removal/addition outcomes; the paper's explicit qualitative summary of positive CAA is retained in r17. The continuous-score gain and null-model comparisons are excluded because they use a first-token proxy rather than semantic refusal.

untested.parts: Preservation of other capabilities. Ablation continued during decoding (formal runs are prefill-only). All-layer or original-style addition (only single-site CAA at α≤1).

missing.what: Correct per-cell Δd′ and ΔF for all-layer ablation. Gemma 2B WG/XS Δd′ −0.725/−0.477; Gemma 9B −0.788/+0.832; ΔF values are now misplaced in r1–r8.
Per-model ΔF (benign refusal) under CAA +0.5/+1 on each dataset, the direct measure of addition inducing refusal.

record.verdict_notes: The flattened Table 17 orders columns ΔH, ΔF, Δd′, Δc. This was verified by recomputing Gemma 2B WG Δd′ = −0.725 from H .067 and F 0. The reader shifted the columns, so r1–r8 hold ΔF values and r9–r16 hold ΔH values. Qwen cells are tangled in the extraction; the Qwen 7B WG Δd′ ≈ −1.10 was confirmed by recomputation. The weaker removal here may reflect prefill-only ablation rather than a failure of the direction. Tranche is borderline T1/T2 because the intervention scope differs from the original.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test preservation of general capabilities. Formal interventions occur during prompt prefill and are disabled during autoregressive decoding; addition is tested as CAA rather than as an all-layer addition.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration procedure is tested.
No jailbreak attack is tested, and no training against ablation is performed.
The study compares direction-identification objectives and local prompt-specific score gains, but does not test an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of semantic refusal.
It separates harmful and benign refusal rates descriptively, but does not separately measure a harmfulness judgment and a refusal decision.
Directions are constructed separately per checkpoint; there is no cross-language, base-to-instruct, or direction-transfer test.
No refusal-training procedure or training-stage comparison is tested.

relation.reason: Its own ablation and addition results bear on whether removing or adding the diff-in-means direction removes or induces refusal.

tranche.reason: Not the same method and measure. Interventions are prefill-only, CAA is single-site, and a blinded gemini-3.7-flash judge scores XSTest/WildGuardTest with SDT. The stated aim is restating V1 as an 'operational causal approximation'. T2 is the fallback if that framing is set aside.

source_check.notes: Table 17 text is flattened: columns run ΔH, ΔF, Δd′, Δc despite the header, and r14/r16 ΔH values are swapped. Placement was recovered by recomputing d′ from Table 16 and matching Table 7. The pack's verdicts carry no [lN] ids, so no_id_1–3 are in pack order. ICLR 2027 submission under double-blind review; the footer is reviewer boilerplate, not addressed to AI.

statements.correction: Prefill single-site CAA, ΔF (benign refusal): α=+1 gives +0.033 (Qwen 2.5–3B WG) to +0.453 (Gemma 2–9B WG); α=+0.5 gives 0.000 (Qwen 3B WG, Qwen 7B XSTest) to +0.213 (Gemma 9B XSTest). Benign refusal at α=+1: Gemma .42–.48, Qwen .07–.22.
statements.problem: The low end of 'about +0.05' is wrong. At α=+1 the smallest rise is +0.033, and at α=+0.5 some cells show no rise.

statements.correction: Also Gemma 2–9B XSTest prefill ablation: harmful refusal .973→.860. Measure: blinded gemini-3.7-flash semantic-refusal judge.
